findings.what: Successful promotion can delete the retained attempt workspace while leaving the interrupted-promotion marker, so restart blocks for manual repair but points the journalist at a workspace that no longer exists.
findings.why: promote_workspace persists the marker, applies live writes, seals state, then calls discard_workspace(workspace) at line 40 before unlinking the marker at line 41. A process termination or machine crash after workspace deletion and before marker unlink leaves promotion.json present but destroys the exact workspace the fail-closed startup contract promises to retain. recover_interrupted_promotion then accepts the marker and records a blocked_reason naming <attempt_path>/workspace without checking that it survived. This is the explicitly covered interruption boundary, not a request for automatic rollback: live files may remain as-is, but the inspection workspace must survive whenever the marker survives. Unlink the marker after sealed state and before ordinary workspace cleanup, so any unlink failure or earlier interruption retains both marker and workspace; a later interruption may leave only harmless stale workspace.

evidence.output: The supplied scan covered all 25 src/anomaly files and recommended REVIEW: six high regex hits, no critical findings, two scanner gaps, no dependency vulnerabilities, gitleaks output parse failure, and absent optional semgrep. The six hits were ast.literal_eval plus five interpolated DuckDB statements.

All six scanner hits are false positives after reachability review. ast.literal_eval is restricted to quoted scalar parsing and cannot execute calls. DuckDB PRAGMA values are positive integers after explicit bool/type/range validation. Prepared table IDs are generated as tbl_ plus a SHA-256 digest, enumerated view names are internal, and profile rejects IDs not matching tbl_[0-9a-f]{64} before interpolation. Detector connections are read-only with external access disabled.

The marker is written before promotion and validated to a fixed phase, bounded integer attempt, and derived relative attempt path. Recovery only writes the blocked state and does not consume legacy entries/backups or mutate registered live outputs. The decisive ordering is line 39 write_state, line 40 discard_workspace(workspace), line 41 marker_path.unlink, creating a reachable marker-without-workspace interruption state.

Public workflow startup calls resume_case before resolving the root or reading the marker; resume_case recursively rejects symlinks, special files, executable artifacts, and symlinked ancestors. Direct run_attempts performs the same whole-case scan before its first state/attempt write and re-scans the isolated workspace after the owner returns. Fixed registry write paths are validated as relative and unique before promotion. No path-escape exploit was found.

Owners execute only in copied attempt workspaces. Owner and validation exceptions delete the disposable workspace, retain three relative failure records, and pass exception text through credential redaction before state, failure.json, and event persistence. The changed tests cover partial P5 drafts and invalid multi-source batches with unchanged live outputs and no rollback material.

Dynamic P5/P6 execution remains bound to fixed installed owner paths and owner kinds. P6 enforces structured review output plus canonical reviewer separation from Gate A, and P7 separates Gate B from the reviewer. Report text is credential-redacted, HTML-escaped, Markdown metacharacter-escaped, URL-colon-neutralized, and collapsed to one line; the inert-Markdown test covers links, HTML images, standalone URLs, and forged headings. Manual XSS/Markdown coverage closes the scanner's XSS gap.
